title: Onboard a team
lead: One form creates the namespace, three policies (admin, developer, reader) and the LDAP roles that map your domain groups onto them. Optionally it also lets chosen Kubernetes ServiceAccounts log in. Everything is created together or not at all.

team.title: Team
team.name: Namespace name
team.nameHint: Lowercase letters, digits and dashes; "/" groups names (team-a/project-x). Cannot be changed later.
team.ttlHint: Optional, e.g. 30m or 8h. Empty = server default.

groups.title: Domain groups
groups.hint: Enter group names or full DNs exactly as the directory returns them (CN=payments-dev,OU=Groups,DC=bank,DC=local). A person in several groups gets the highest level. At least one group is required.
groups.adminHint: Read, write, delete and list secrets; view policies
groups.developerHint: Read, write and list secrets (no delete)

k8s.title: Kubernetes workloads
k8s.hint: Optional. Lets a ServiceAccount log in on its own (injector, CSI). The operator needs nothing here: it uses its own identity and the namespace annotation shown after creation.

plan.title: What will be created
plan.empty: Fill in the form and press Preview. Nothing is changed until you create.
plan.name: Name

errors.name: Use lowercase letters, digits and dashes
errors.ttl: Use a number with s, m or h, e.g. 8h

done.title: Team {{name}} is ready
done.next: Last step on the cluster side: annotate each Kubernetes namespace so the operator reads this team's secrets. Run it on the matching cluster:
done.noHints: No Kubernetes bindings were added, so there is nothing to annotate yet. When the team deploys TuckSecret resources, annotate its namespace with tuck.io/tuck-namespace.
